title: MoSJE and Ministry of Defence Join Hands to Strengthen Welfare of Senior Citizens in Cantonment Areas Across The Country
subtitle:
MoU Signed between DoSJE and DGDE in the Presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar
New Day Care Centres to be Established in Cantonments; Existing Centres and Senior Citizen Homes to be Supported and Expanded under AVYAY
Youth from Cantonment Areas to Receive Training as Geriatric Caregivers; Partnership to Promote Dignified, Secure and Active Ageing through Better Care and Community Participation
body_text: The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Directorate General Defence Estates (DGDE), Ministry of Defence, in the National Capital here today, to strengthen the welfare and well-being of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas. The MoU was signed in the presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar. Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Director General, Defence Estates, Smt. Shobha Gupta, Joint Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, and other senior officers from both Ministries were present on the occasion. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was formally exchanged between Ms Kajal Singh, Director, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri Mane AmitKumar B., Deputy Director General (Cantonments Division-II), Directorate General Defence Estates, Ministry of Defence, in the presence of the Union Ministers and senior officials of both Ministries. Speaking at the event, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar reaffirmed the Government's commitment under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to ensuring dignified, secure and active ageing for every senior citizen. Dr Kumar highlighted that through the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY), the Ministry is supporting Senior Citizen Homes, Day Care Centres, Geriatric caregiver training, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens ( ELDERLINE – 14567 ) and other welfare initiatives. He stated that the MoU would extend better care, welfare services and opportunities for active ageing to senior citizens living in Cantonment areas. The Minister also appealed to citizens, particularly youth, officers and staff of Cantonment Boards and members of Cantonment communities, to register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers. Launched on November 4, 2026, alongside the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, Vayo SAATHI encourages citizens aged 18 years and above to spend time with senior citizens, assist them in their daily needs and facilitate their access to welfare schemes, the Minister said. Emphasising the importance of inter-generational companionship, Dr. Virendra Kumar said, “Every Vayo SAATHI is a bridge between generations. I urge citizens to register as a Vayo SAATHI and become a companion to our elders. ” Dr Kumar reiterated the Government’s commitment to the welfare of senior citizens and enumerated the initiatives taken by MoSJE, including the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), to improve the quality of life of the elderly. He stated that the MoU marks an important step towards strengthening the support system for senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas by ensuring access to better care, welfare services and opportunities for active and dignified ageing. Addressing the gathering, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that senior citizens are not merely members of families but also carriers of experience, traditions and social values. He observed that their guidance and wisdom would play an important role in the journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047. Shri Singh said their experience, wisdom and guidance will be invaluable in the journey to create peaceful, harmonious and knowledgeable societies. Highlighting their lifelong contribution to building families, society and the nation, he termed it a social and moral responsibility to ensure that they are accorded respect, security and a sense of belonging. Recalling the Indian ethos of “Matru Devo Bhava, Pitru Devo Bhava”, he emphasised that caring for senior citizens is a social and moral responsibility as well as a national duty, extending beyond the boundaries of individual families. While acknowledging the progress made in senior citizen welfare, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the need for continuous improvement in the delivery of services to the elderly. The Raksha Mantri also called for regular social audits of Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes to assess the quality of services, identify areas requiring further improvement and address gaps through continuous monitoring. In his closing remarks, Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sudhansh Pant said that the MoU represents a shared commitment towards ensuring companionship, dignity and care for senior citizens closer to their homes. Joint Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, stated that a Joint Working Group would work closely with DGDE to ensure that the new Day Care Centres become operational and caregiver training programmes commence in the identified Cantonments at the earliest. The MoU aims to promote the welfare of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY). The partnership envisages the establishment of new Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes with residential facilities of 25/50-bed capacity, wherever feasible. It will also support and strengthen existing facilities run by Cantonment Boards. Under the arrangement, DGDE will facilitate the provision of infrastructure, premises and basic civic amenities, while the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will extend financial assistance, technical guidance, training and operational support. The partnership will also focus on training youth from Cantonment areas as geriatric caregivers, along with awareness generation, skill development and promotion of inter-generational bonding. A Joint Working Group will be constituted to monitor implementation, facilitate coordination and ensure effective execution of the initiatives. The MoU will remain valid for five years, with a provision for renewal. The MoU comes at a significant juncture as the Defence Estates Department marks its centenary, commemorating 100 years since its establishment in 1926. The partnership reflects the expanding role of the Defence Estates Department from administration to community welfare. By bringing together the infrastructure and civic facilities of Cantonment Boards with the policy, technical and financial support of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the initiative exemplifies the Whole of Government approach towards ensuring the welfare, dignity and well-being of senior citizens.
